generation_reason: Generation 1 evaluated speech-native/full-duplex model source eligibility. Generation 2 isolates the orthogonal acoustic echo cancellation/playback-reference prerequisite needed to interpret later simultaneous speaker+microphone barge-in measurements.
question: Is there a current source-supported local acoustic echo cancellation path with an explicit playback/reference stream that can make later microphone-vs-speaker full-duplex German barge-in measurements interpretable?

observed: PipeWire documents libpipewire-module-echo-cancel as an echo-cancellation module.
The documented topology has four streams: microphone capture, an application-fed sink carrying the signal to cancel, playback to the speaker, and a source exposing echo-cancelled capture.
The sink/reference stream and capture stream are correlated so the sink signal can be removed from capture.
The documented default AEC library is aec/libspa-aec-webrtc.
EchoCanceller3 exposes separate render analysis and capture processing surfaces.
AnalyzeRender stores an internal copy of the render signal while ProcessCapture removes echo from capture.
speex_echo_cancellation takes microphone recording and the signal played to the speaker as separate inputs and returns the near-end signal with echo removed.
speex_echo_playback explicitly supplies frames queued to the sound card to the echo canceller.

architecture_inference: A later F2 full-duplex test can be made causally interpretable by routing synthesized assistant audio through an AEC reference/playback path and feeding ASR/turn detection from the echo-cancelled capture path.
PipeWire provides a particularly direct Linux integration candidate because it exposes virtual playback and capture nodes around the AEC engine.
